title: Verification
subtitle: Run queries on the reachability graph: CTL formulas, reachability, distances, circuits and predicates.
selectFile: Select a .pnt file to run queries.
marking.label: Target marking
marking.help: One value per place, in the order shown below, separated by commas.
marking.noPlaces: Could not determine the places of this net.
marking.alreadyInitial: This is the initial marking itself.
marking.notReachableDesc: No firing sequence from M₀ produces this token distribution.
algebraic.hint: The algebraic test uses invariants and the state equation. It can prove a marking unreachable, but never that it is reachable.
algebraic.onlyAlgebraic: The graph check is unavailable for this net, but the algebraic and coverability tests still work.
algebraic.unreachable: Not reachable — proved without the graph
algebraic.byInvariant: A P-invariant keeps this weighted sum constant in every reachable marking:
algebraic.invariantValues: It equals {initial} at M₀ but {target} at the target.
algebraic.byStateEquation: No firing-count vector x ≥ 0 satisfies the state equation M = M₀ + C·x.
algebraic.farkas: Certificate (Farkas): this weighting is never negative for any firing, yet it is negative for the change from M₀ to the target:
algebraic.possibleDesc: No algebraic test refutes it. That is not a proof of reachability: it only means the necessary conditions hold.
algebraic.parikh: Firing counts that solve the state equation:
coverage.unsupported: The coverability test is not valid for nets with inhibitor arcs or immediate transitions, because firing stops being monotone.
coverage.coveredDesc: Some reachable marking has at least this many tokens in every place.
coverage.notCoveredDesc: No reachable marking has at least this many tokens in every place.
coverage.unbounded: The net is unbounded, so this answer comes from the coverability graph, which always terminates.
coverage.omegaPath: The path goes through ω (unbounded growth): it shows how the places grow, not a literal firing sequence.
coverage.exactPath: Shortest path in the coverability graph from M₀ to a covering marking.
coverage.initialCovers: The initial marking already covers it.
distances.fromHelp: Distances are counted in firings, starting from this marking (M₀ by default).
distances.toHint: Optional. Leave it empty to see only the distances from the source.
distances.explain: Eccentricity is the largest distance from the source; the diameter is the largest distance between any two states.
distances.unreachable: {count} states cannot be reached from the source.
distances.diameterSkipped: The graph is too large to scan every pair, so the diameter was skipped.
distances.histogram: States at each distance from the source
distances.noPath: The target cannot be reached from the source.
circuits.kind.shortest.title: Shortest
circuits.kind.shortest.desc: All circuits with the minimum number of firings. Fast, even on large graphs.
circuits.kind.all.title: All, up to a length
circuits.kind.all.desc: Every circuit up to a maximum length, shortest first, with the count per length.
circuits.kind.longest.title: Longest
circuits.kind.longest.desc: The longest circuit found before the time limit. Finding the true longest is a hard problem.
circuits.throughHint: Optional. Leave it empty to search the whole graph.
circuits.budgetNote: A graph can have billions of circuits, so the search is bounded by a time limit and a list size.
circuits.none: No circuit of this kind exists.
circuits.noneYet: No circuit found before the time limit.
circuits.partial: The time limit stopped the search, so the counts are lower bounds.
circuits.partialLongest: The time limit stopped the search. A longer circuit may exist.
circuits.firstOnlyNote: Stopped at the first circuit, as requested.
circuits.closed: The circuit returns to its first marking:
circuits.notFired: {count} transitions never fire on this circuit
predicates.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it by hand
predicates.enabled.title: Enabledness predicate
predicates.enabled.desc: True in every state where at least one of the chosen transitions is enabled: its input places hold the arc weights and its inhibitor places are below their thresholds. Priorities are not applied.
predicates.states.title: Predicate from a set of states
predicates.states.desc: True exactly in the listed states of the reachability graph. Each state becomes a conjunction that fixes every place.
predicates.states.label: States (graph ids)
predicates.states.hint: Use the M numbers from the Graphs tab. Ranges work: 0, 3, 5-8.
predicates.states.invalid: Could not read the list. Use numbers, M numbers or ranges such as 5-8.
predicates.states.needsGraph: This needs the exact reachability graph, which is unavailable for this net.
predicates.result.enabled: Ready to use in a query. The CTL standard line shows how it expands.
predicates.pdcDesc: The same predicate in the text format INA writes and reads.
placeBound.hint: Decides whether one place can hold unboundedly many tokens, without building the full reachability graph (stubborn-set Karp–Miller tree, Schmidt 1999). Works even when other places are unbounded.
placeBound.unknownDesc: The node limit ({count}) was reached before a verdict. Raise the state limit in the graph settings and try again.
deadTransition.hint: A transition is dead when no reachable marking enables it. Decided with stubborn sets, without building the full graph; when it can fire, a shortest sequence that enables it is shown (Schmidt 1999).
deadTransition.deadDesc: No reachable marking enables it (explored {count} markings).
deadTransition.unknownDesc: The node limit ({count}) was reached before a verdict. Raise the state limit in the graph settings and try again.
deadTransition.enabledInitially: It is enabled at the initial marking.
deadTransition.witness: Shortest sequence that enables it ({count} firings): {path}
